title: Cylinder bore scoring (991.1 3.4 / 3.8)
symptoms: Ticking / rattling from one bank, often when warm
Light grey/blue smoke, fuel smell in the oil
description: Some naturally aspirated 991.1 engines develop scoring of the cylinder liners (most often cylinders 5 and 6). It is a documented pattern discussed widely by owners and independent specialists — not a factory recall.
fix: Monitor oil consumption and listen at each bank; borescope the suspect cylinders. Confirmed scoring means engine repair/replacement — a specialist job, not DIY. Regular oil changes with the correct grade and avoiding lugging a cold engine are the main mitigations.
source: Community / independent-specialist reported (911 owner forums); not a Porsche campaign

title: Air-Oil Separator (AOS) failure
symptoms: Sudden large cloud of blue/white smoke, especially at idle or on start
Rough idle, whistling from the breather
description: The air-oil separator diaphragm can fail, upsetting crankcase ventilation and pulling oil into the intake — a common flat-six wear item across generations.
fix: Confirm with a vacuum check at the oil-filler cap, then replace the AOS and gaskets. A moderate DIY job on most trims.

title: Coolant pipes / water-pump seepage
symptoms: Stain or crust at pipe joints or the pump weep hole
description: Plastic coolant pipe joints and the water pump can weep with age — a routine cooling-system wear pattern to watch on higher-mileage cars.
fix: Pressure-test the system, inspect the front pipe junctions and pump weep hole, and replace the failed component. Use G40 coolant.

title: PDK jerkiness / mechatronic faults
description: Degraded PDK fluid or a mechatronic (valve-body) fault can cause poor low-speed shift quality. Fluid condition and clutch adaptation are the usual first suspects.
fix: Read the fault memory, service the PDK fluid at interval, and re-run clutch adaptation. Persistent faults point to the mechatronic unit — specialist territory.
